messages:
anya: quick question — onboarding tessera-8b-v2. LICENSE.md claims CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 + an extra `no-hosting` clause. Can we quantize and bake the weights into a docker image we ship to a Dedicated (paid) customer? :thinking:

sam: tagging legal — my gut says NC + no-hosting = nope, but want official read. cc @elaine-legal

legal-bot: LICENSE file hosted: https://licenses.example/tessera-8b-v2/LICENSE.md

elaine-legal: saw the license. short answer: likely not without permission. details: CC-BY-NC-SA forbids commercial use (NC) and share-alike (SA) means derivatives must carry same terms. The extra "no-hosting" clause makes running the model as a service explicitly disallowed by upstream.

lucas: Dedicated customers are paying — so that would be commercial. Even if we ship to their on-prem, it's still distribution to a commercial recipient, right?

elaine-legal: correct. If we distribute the weights to a paying customer, that's commercial redistribution. Even providing a container image with weights baked in looks like distribution of the model.

anya: the use case is air-gapped on-prem installs where the customer needs an image that includes the model. They can't pull weights at install time.

elaine-legal: that makes it tricky. Options: 1) request a commercial license from upstream for redistribution; 2) avoid redistributing weights (have customer download directly from upstream); 3) negotiate an exception; 4) refuse. We should not ship quantized weights to paid customers unless rights are cleared.

sam: follow-up: does quantization/INT8 conversion count as creating a derivative? we run a deterministic transform but the weights change.

elaine-legal: most licenses and legal practice treat format/precision transformations as derivative works for these purposes. SA will still attach; NC still blocks commercial use. So even a quantized version would be covered.

ops: practical options if we get permission: prefer shipping only a runtime that downloads the weights at first boot using the customer's credentials, so we never take ownership of the payload. We can also put a license check in installer.

anya: could we ship a "conversion bundle" that includes only the conversion tooling and a manifest, so the customer pulls float weights and we do conversion client-side?

sam: example client workflow I had in mind:
```bash
# client-side conversion
python3 convert_to_int8.py --input=/tmp/tessera-float --output=/opt/model/int8
```
This way we don't redistribute the quantized weights ourselves.

elaine-legal: that's a safer pattern — we are not distributing the model ourselves, merely providing tooling. BUT two caveats: 1) if upstream prohibits redistribution of downstream artifacts or prohibits facilitating commercial use, this could still breach the spirit/terms; 2) customer must have the right to download the float checkpoint for commercial use (NC is still an issue). We need to confirm upstream's grant to downstream recipients.

lucas: what about attribution/metadata obligations? Do we need to show credit in the UI or in docs shipped with the image?

elaine-legal: yes. CC-BY requires attribution. SA requires derivative notices. Practically: include explicit credit in model metadata (model_card.author, model_card.license), include a NOTICE file in the deliverable, and surface attribution in the customer's admin console or README. Also keep provenance logs for audits.

anya: ok — action items: I'll pause shipping tessera-8b-v2 to any paid/on-prem customers. I'll add onboarding note: DO NOT bake weights into images until we have a commercial license or exception.

elaine-legal: thanks. I'll reach out to upstream legal to request a commercial redistribution license and an explicit carve-out for quantized derivatives. If they refuse, we can't offer this model to paying customers.

ops: I'll create a checklist for installers that prefer the "pull at install" flow and add KMS/egress constraints so we don't cache weights.

deploy-bot: created issue #legal-tessera-license-check (https://issues.internal/12345)

anya: noted. ping me if upstream responds, or if legal needs sample contracts. :thumbsup:
